thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert — canary deploy rolling out to 10% of traffic (deploy/2026-03-15T16:04Z). Error rate on hosted-inference increased to 8% (5xx) over last 1m. Auto-rollback did NOT trigger (timeout).

sre-oncall: I'm on it. taking pager. starting investigation.

Emma: grabbing logs from canary hosts, will share top-5 stack traces.

Raj: noticed increased p95 latency as well, looks correlated with requests that hit model cache miss.

Jamie Ops: can we pause traffic to canary group? what's current rollout percentage?

sre-oncall: Current split: 10% canary, 90% stable. I don't have an immediate kill-switch in the deploy pipeline because of a gating bug — manual flag flip only.

Product Ops: Customer-facing impact: several enterprise customers report request timeouts and degraded SLAs. CS is triaging.

CS Lead: I have a thread with 3 customers experiencing 503s. Escalating to priority.

Emma: paste logs: ```
2026-03-15T16:05:12Z ERROR inference-host-12 request_id=abc123 model=redwood-13b seq=512 OOM while allocating KV cache
2026-03-15T16:05:13Z WARN inference-host-14 cache-miss slow-path 450ms
```

Raj: kv-cache growth on the canary variant looks exponential for longer contexts. suspect quantized kernel regression from latest build.

Jamie Ops: Ok, plan: 1) Drain traffic from canary back to stable 2) If drain fails, flip feature flag to divert 100% 3) If flag flip risky, manual rollback of canary deployment to previous image. Who will run the flag flip?

sre-oncall: I'll run the flag flip in 1st step. Hopping into infra console now.

Incident Bot: :information_source: Note: automated rollback disabled for this job due to infra bug #INC-4312. Manual action required.

Emma: I pushed a quick canary-only metric to monitor KV allocations. Will update every 30s.

sre-oncall: Starting traffic drain to stable via routing policy. Command used: ```
# drain canary group
redwoodctl rollout traffic --target canary --percent 0 --grace-period 60s --reason \"emergency drain\"
```

sre-oncall: drain initiated. monitoring logs...

Jamie Ops: CS notified customers: "We're diverting traffic to a stable variant to mitigate 503s. We'll update in 15m."

Emma: after 30s, 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 1.2% for stable. Canary still shows 9% until fully drained.

Raj: drain seems stuck at 4% canary; some sessions pinned because of sticky routing (session affinity). Need to evict sessions.

sre-oncall: evicting sticky sessions via: ```
redwoodctl session kill --label canary --older-than 5m
```

sre-oncall: sessions evicted. canary traffic now at 0.3%. attempting final cutoff.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Canary traffic < 1%. Stable metrics returning to baseline.

Emma: verifying model health on canary hosts — collecting core dumps and disabling the new kernel. We'll prepare a rollback image with previous kernel.

Raj: automated rollback would have used the prior image and kernel, but the pipeline didn't trigger. After this, we should add a guard to prevent canary with changed kernel from promoting.

Jamie Ops: Do we want to do a manual rollback of the canary image to be safe (so any lingering endpoints are identical)? Or decommission canary hosts?

sre-oncall: Manual rollback executed (canary image -> redwood-inference:v2026-02-28). Command: ```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service inference --revision v2026-02-28 --scope canary --force
```

sre-oncall: rollback completed. verifying: healthchecks passing, no OOMs in last 2m.

CS Lead: customers updated: one enterprise account asked for incident postmortem. They'll need ETA.

Product Ops: we'll prepare a short post-incident note: root cause likely kernel selection change causing KV cache bloat on long contexts. Action items: revert kernel change in next PR, add automated rollback guard, fix auto-rollback condition.

Emma: I'll attach the problematic kernel diff and sample core dump to the ticket.

Raj: Verification checklist done: 
- traffic drained ✅
- sticky sessions evicted ✅
- rollback applied ✅
- stable SLAs restored ✅

sre-oncall: handing back to normal oncall. If anyone sees residual 5xx, ping me.

Jamie Ops: great work. tagging for postmortem: assign to Emma/Raj, deadline EOD tomorrow for initial write-up.

Incident Bot: :tada: Incident resolved (severity: sev2). Closing thread in 30m unless new messages.
